name: Wazn
description: A star 27 parsecs away, 10 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 27628: radius 10.487 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 46.438 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.054) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 27628: effective temperature 4656 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.069)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 2.59 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 8 published values span log g 2.48 to 2.8, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 27628: distance 26.731 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.003), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 27 parsecs away, 10 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 46 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,656 K, so 10.487 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 27628: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Beta Columbae
quotes.card: Beta Columbae is the second-brightest star in the southern constellation of Columba.
quotes.introduction: It has the proper name Wazn ; Beta Columbae is its Bayer designation, which is Latinized from β Columbae, and abbreviated Beta Col or β Col.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 2887731882922767744 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
